package_info.why_malicious: These packages are typosquatted variants of popular Roblox developer modules, containing obfuscated JavaScript that downloads and executes infostealer malware (Skuld and Blank Grabber) from external sources. The code enables remote code execution and exfiltration of sensitive data, posing severe risks to users.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (upon package use or installation)
execution_context.file_location: main entry JavaScript file (e.g., index.js or main.js) of the malicious npm package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code defines URLs pointing to malicious executables hosted on GitHub, setting up for subsequent download and execution of malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hardcoded URLs to external executables, especially from a non-official GitHub repository, are a strong indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not reference or download executables from untrusted external sources, especially not malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate updaters or installers may reference official binaries for updates, but only from trusted, verified sources.
key_indicators: References to known malware (Skuld Infostealer, Blank Grabber)
Use of GitHub as a malware hosting platform

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (upon package use or installation)
execution_context.file_location: main entry JavaScript file (e.g., index.js or main.js) of the malicious npm package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code downloads a file from a specified URL using PowerShell and then executes it, enabling arbitrary code execution and malware deployment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated download and execution of remote binaries is a classic malware delivery technique, especially when obfuscated and triggered without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should not execute PowerShell commands to download and run external executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers or updaters may use similar logic, but only for trusted, signed binaries and with user awareness.
key_indicators: Use of PowerShell to download and execute files
No user interaction or consent required

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious npm package, triggering the execution of the main JavaScript file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded and begins execution.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code defines URLs to malware executables hosted on GitHub.
The downloadAndRun function is invoked, downloading the malware executables to the victim's system using PowerShell.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware binaries are present on the victim's machine.

attack_chain.action: The downloaded executables (Skuld Infostealer and Blank Grabber) are executed, compromising the system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware runs, stealing credentials and sensitive data.

attack_chain.action: Stolen data is exfiltrated to the threat actor via Discord webhooks or Telegram.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive information; compromise complete.

behavioral_signatures: npm package executes PowerShell commands at install or import time
Download and execution of Windows executables from non-official GitHub repositories
Obfuscated JavaScript that references external URLs for .exe files
Automated invocation of exec/execAsync with suspicious command strings
file_indicators: Presence of hardcoded URLs to github.com/zvydev/code/raw/main/*.exe
References to RobloxPlayerLauncher.exe and cmd.exe in package code
Obfuscated or minified JavaScript in main entry files of npm packages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for execution of PowerShell or shell commands that download and run external executables, especially from non-official sources. Flag packages containing hardcoded URLs to suspicious GitHub repositories or .exe files. Detect obfuscated JavaScript that invokes exec/execAsync with download and execution logic. Monitor for outbound connections to known C2 channels such as Discord webhooks and Telegram. Use static analysis to identify packages with references to known malware filenames or suspicious network destinations.
